recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a dead-man's-switch heartbeat for nightly-sync: either the healthchecks.io free tier or a self-hosted equivalent in a Docker container on the Synology. The script would ping it with curl at start and end, and send a separate failure notification when it exits non-zero.

labels.Requirements and who asked: you want to be notified when the job fails, not read logs, and asked about centralizing logs toward that end.
labels.Deleted: full ELK/Loki-style log aggregation stack, Dockerizing everything — neither one would have caught this specific failure mode and you don't want to read logs anyway.
labels.Bottleneck: the missing check isn't "where do logs live," it's "nobody/nothing watches for the job not running at all."
labels.Checked myself: from what you told me — crash was pre-email, at startup, four nights straight, nothing else alerts on this job today.

note: The heartbeat is a small fix, but the final recommendation also offers a self-hosted Docker container on the Synology as an option and adds a separate failure notification, and the dead-man's-switch is already proposed in the second paragraph, before the four labelled lines.
